findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the empty-reason fallback: when `force` bypasses the close gate with no `reason` supplied, preserve the existing `"(no reason given)"` placeholder in the FORCE_CLOSE audit comment (transition_close.py:518-520).
evidence: transition.py:662 `force_close=(force_reason or "(no reason given)") if force else ""`
transition_close.py:520 `f'... Reason: "{force_close}". ...'`
Plan says the note 'comes from the already-established separate reason parameter' but reason defaults to empty
findings.finding: The plan does not specify the empty-reason fallback for the force-close audit note. Today a bare CLI `--force` defaults force_close to the placeholder `"(no reason given)"` (transition.py:662), so the FORCE_CLOSE audit comment (transition_close.py:518-520) never renders an empty reason. Under the new plan the note comes from `reason`; a bare `--force` with no `--reason` leaves `reason` empty, degrading the audit comment to `Reason: ""`.
findings.location: Approach: 'recording reason as the force-close audit note'; transition_close.py:512-520
scenarios: Operator runs `transition abc1 closed --force` with no --reason under the completion-verification gate
findings.suggested_fix: In transition_close.py, compute the audit note as `reason or "(no reason given)"` at the `if force:` branch so a bare force retains the placeholder.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Expand the transition.py scope to name the internal seam derived from a symbol-reference sweep: the `_parse_flags` `--force=<reason>` branch (L179-181), `transition_compute`'s own `force_close`/`force_reason` params (L237-238) and its forwarding to `close_ticket`/`_cascade_open_parent` (L354, L374, L413-419), and the start-work note re-sourced from `reason` (L341-342, L662) — not just the usage/help text.

findings.finding: The plan removes the `force_close` param and drops the CLI `--force=<reason>` inline form, but its transition.py inventory omits the internal `transition_compute` seam that carries these symbols: `transition_compute` has its OWN `force_close: str` param (transition.py L238) plus a `force_reason: str` param (L237) which is the mechanism that carries the inline `--force=<reason>` value, and `_parse_flags` (L179-181) is the code that parses `--force=<value>` into `force_reason`. The plan's transition.py scope is worded only as CLI flag/usage-text changes ('--force bare bool only ... update usage/help') and its patch-site list (close_precheck.py ~566, transition_close.py ~440, lib param) does not name these. force_reason seam (L341-342, L354, L413-419) left unaddressed: the start-work gate audit note keeps drawing from force_reason rather than the `reason` param the plan designates, so the intended consolidation onto `reason` silently under-delivers on the start-work path.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the CLI back-out/rationale for the asymmetry: either justify the immediate --force=<reason> hard removal (operator ruling + 24f7 precedent) as an explicit clean-break choice, or specify a guided error/deprecation message when the inline form is passed.
evidence: Lib path: 'a call passing force_close="<r>" WARNs and is mapped to force=True, reason="<r>", scheduled for removal.'
CLI path: '--force becomes a bare boolean (drop the --force=<reason> inline form)' with no deprecation alias or rejection-message plan.
Plan notes the prior --force-close spelling 'was already retired as a clean break in 24f7' as precedent.
findings.finding: The lib force_close removal gets an expand-contract migration (a deprecation alias that WARNs and maps to force+reason), but the CLI --force=<reason> inline-form removal is an immediate hard break with no stated grace period or back-out path; the asymmetry is not explicitly justified.
scenarios: An operator script invoking `transition ... --force=some-reason` breaks with a raw parse error rather than a guided deprecation message.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a note that the CLI inline-form removal is a deliberate clean break (per the 2026-08-18 operator ruling and the 24f7 --force-close precedent), and specify that `--force=<reason>` now produces a clear usage error directing callers to `--force --reason=<text>`.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the error/guidance shown when a user supplies the retired `--force=<reason>` inline form (point them to `--reason`), and assert that message in the interface test.
evidence: 'The CLI `--force=<reason>` inline form is no longer accepted; bare `--force` + `--reason` is the path (interface test).'
The interface test asserts non-acceptance but the plan does not describe the error message shown to a user migrating from the old form.
findings.finding: The plan drops the CLI `--force=<reason>` inline form and asserts it is 'no longer accepted' but does not specify the non-happy-path user experience for operators who still type the old form — whether they get a clear migration error pointing to `--reason` or an opaque argparse failure.
findings.location: Scope — 'CLI: `--force` becomes a bare boolean (drop the `--force=<reason>` inline form)'
scenarios: An operator with muscle memory runs `transition ... --force="needed by ops"`: they see a raw arg-parse error with no hint to use `--reason`, and cannot tell how to migrate.
